lesson.topicTitle: 1. Structure, Bonding & Introduction to Organic Chemistry

specAnchors.text: be able to draw and name the structural isomers of alkanes and cycloalkanes with up to six carbon atoms

primer.text: One molecular formula can build several real compounds: structural isomers wire the same atoms differently. Branching shortens the longest chain (pentane against 2,2-dimethylpropane); moving a functional group re-addresses it (butan-1-ol against butan-2-ol); and a hunt protocol - draw, decide stereo or structural, classify - counts them all, from four dibromopropanes to two C4H10 skeletons.

modules.title: Same formula, different molecule
modules.opening: Structural isomers are compounds with one molecular formula but different structural formulae: same atoms, wired differently. Propene and cyclopropane both count three carbons and six hydrogens, yet one is an open alkene and the other a ring. The two flavours of structural isomerism to master are chain isomerism and positional isomerism.
keyPoints: Structural isomers share the same molecular formula but differ in structural formulae.
Propene and cyclopropane are isomers - both C3H6, one open-chained, one ringed.
Chain isomerism arises when the longest hydrocarbon chain differs.
Positional isomerism arises when the same functional group sits on different carbons.
Counting atoms never separates isomers - only the bonding arrangement does.

low.restatement: Same ingredient list, different assembly: isomers fool the formula but not the structure.
low.analogy: The same LEGO bricks built as a tower or an arch - identical inventory, different model.
low.examPointer: Always demonstrate isomerism by writing both structural formulae - the difference is the proof.

medium.restatement: Isomerism is a connectivity distinction: identical molecular formulae with different bonding arrangements, classified by WHAT differs - the skeleton (chain) or the functional group's address (positional) - while the atom inventory stays fixed.
medium.analogy: Two routes on one map between the same towns: identical endpoints (formula), different roads taken (structure).
medium.examPointer: Propene versus cyclopropane is the canonical demo pair - quote both C3H6 formulae and their differing structures.

modules.title: Chain isomerism: the branching disease
modules.opening: Chain isomerism keeps the molecular formula and changes the longest hydrocarbon chain - branching is the cause. Pentane's straight five-carbon chain and 2,2-dimethylpropane's three-carbon backbone with two methyl branches hold identical atom inventories yet name different longest chains: five versus three.
keyPoints: Chain isomerism means same molecular formula but different longest hydrocarbon chain.
Pentane and 2,2-dimethylpropane are chain isomers of the same formula.
Pentane's longest chain runs five carbons; 2,2-dimethylpropane's runs three, with two methyl branches.
The atom inventory is unchanged - only the chain architecture differs.

low.restatement: Same atoms, different skeleton: branch the chain and the longest run shortens, giving a chain isomer.
low.analogy: The same rope re-knotted: straight it spans five marks; knotted mid-way its longest straight run is three.
low.examPointer: State both longest-chain lengths when demonstrating chain isomerism - the numbers are the evidence.

medium.restatement: Chain isomerism relocates carbons from the main chain into branches: the molecular formula is conserved while the maximum contiguous run of carbons contracts, which is why pentane (C5 chain) and 2,2-dimethylpropane (C3 chain plus two methyls) qualify.
medium.analogy: A motorway re-routed through side streets: same total tarmac, shorter longest straight stretch.
medium.examPointer: 'Caused by branching' is the quotable cause - pair it with the longest-chain contrast.

modules.title: Positional isomerism and the isomer hunt
modules.opening: Positional isomers carry the same functional group on different carbons: butan-1-ol and butan-2-ol both hold four carbons, ten hydrogens and one oxygen - only the -OH's address moves. The hunting protocol then generalises: draw the structure, decide structural versus stereo, and walk the checklist - functional group? chain? positional? Dibromopropane yields four positional isomers; C4H10 yields two chain isomers.
keyPoints: Positional isomers differ in the position of the same functional group.
Butan-1-ol and butan-2-ol both hold 4 carbons, 10 hydrogens and one oxygen - the OH moves from carbon 1 to carbon 2.
The hunt protocol: draw the structure, decide structural versus stereo, then check functional group, chain, positional in turn.
Dibromopropane, C3H6Br2, shows positional isomerism - the two bromines sit on different carbons - yielding 4 isomers.
C4H10 shows chain isomerism only, yielding 2 isomers: butane and 2-methylpropane.

low.restatement: Same group, different address: slide the functional group along the chain and each stop is a positional isomer. To hunt all isomers, draw, decide the type, then walk the checklist.
low.analogy: The same shop sign hung on different doors of one street - same shop, different address.
low.examPointer: Quote the atom inventory when demonstrating positional isomers - C4H10O for both butanols - then point at the differing carbon.

medium.restatement: The positional mechanism relocates a functional group across equivalent-or-not carbons while conserving the formula; the hunt protocol then enumerates systematically - restricted rotation splits stereo from structural, and the functional-group/chain/positional checklist classifies each structural case, as dibromopropane's four bromine placements and C4H10's two skeletons show.
medium.analogy: A building survey: first decide whether differences are architectural (structural) or mirror-image (stereo), then audit each floor - group placement, skeleton shape, group address.
medium.examPointer: Walk the checklist in order and answer each step explicitly - marks attach to the reasoning, not just the count.

glossary.definition: One of a set of compounds sharing a molecular formula but differing in structural formula.
Isomerism where the longest hydrocarbon chain differs because of branching.
Isomerism where the same functional group occupies different carbon positions.

workedExample.prompt: How many isomers does dibromopropane, C3H6Br2, have?
steps: Draw the structure: a three-carbon chain bearing two bromines.
No restricted rotation about the C-C bond, so the isomerism is structural.
Functional-group type? No - bromine is the only group available here. Chain type? No - the longest run stops at three carbons. Positional type? Yes - the two bromines can take up different carbons.
The placements 1,1-, 1,2-, 1,3- and 2,2-dibromopropane give four isomers.
